page: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v6 is a high-density, compute-oriented instance within the Dldsv6 series, configured with 128 vCPUs derived from 64 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides dedicated CPU resource allocation alongside 260 MB of Level 3 cache. Advanced hardware extensions include AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8, delivering dedicated vector and matrix processing capabilities without discrete GPU hardware.

The instance is equipped with 256 GB of system RAM, providing an allocation of 2 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features 7559 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD capacity, supporting low-latency scratch disks, operational databases, and caching tiers without relying strictly on remote network volumes. Single-threaded metrics land in the middle tier, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1945.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2076.0. In contrast, multi-threaded execution reaches top-tier throughput, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 103274.51 and large-block memory read bandwidth exceeding 501 GB/sec.

Workload evaluation highlights high efficiency for compute-dense, I/O-intensive services. Benchmarks recorded 146.84 million Redis SET operations per second and 162.64 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference achieves 303.22 tokens per second on 7B models during prompt ingestion via matrix instructions. Given its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and extensive NVMe capacity, the instance is well suited for high-throughput database clusters, parallel code compilation pipelines, data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency web microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v6 is an Intel Xeon 8573C instance featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs, 64 physical cores, and clock frequencies reaching 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with a 1:2 memory ratio, it delivers 256 GB of RAM alongside 7559 GB of bundled NVMe SSD local storage. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix math acceleration, while discrete GPUs are absent. Multi-threaded benchmark testing reflects top-tier performance, producing a PassMark CPU score of 103274.51 and Redis SET performance surpassing 146 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth exceeds 501 GB/sec on uncached reads. The balanced combination of dedicated core density and high-capacity local NVMe storage positions this server for parallel software builds, real-time database operations, web proxy clusters, and large-scale data transformation workloads.
